title: Event-first streaming API for Python chat completions
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: current Python SDK streaming primitives are ad-hoc and force consumers to reimplement common patterns (idempotency, checkpointing, backpressure, structured event handling). Goal: ship an 'event-first' streaming API that treats every token/chunk as a typed event and provides ergonomics for progressive consumption, checkpoints, retries, and graceful fallback to non-streaming.

Scope and deliverables: implement a new high-level API surface (StreamingSession + EventRouter) and a lightweight Event object model (type: 'delta'|'metadata'|'error'|'done', attrs: text, tokens, index, meta). Provide middleware hooks (preprocess, on_event, on_error, on_done), first-class checkpoint/restore helpers, and examples (consumer patterns, fn-calling + streaming, resumable long outputs). Ensure backwards-compatible lower-level iterator is preserved for advanced users. Include comprehensive unit/integration tests and at least two example notebooks: one for server-sent events integration and one for stateful resume after transient network failure.

Design decisions and trade-offs: 1) Represent events as small immutable dataclasses (adds minor allocation overhead but dramatically improves developer ergonomics and type-safety). 2) Default API returns an async iterator of Event objects and a convenience 'on' registration API for callback-style usage. This covers both iterator-first and callback-first consumers. 3) Checkpointing uses a lightweight opaque checkpoint token (string) that encodes last-processed sequence id + KV-cache snapshot pointer; we avoid storing model internals but provide hooks for embedding/summary-based resume for very long contexts. 4) Retry semantics: client-side transparent retry for idempotent requests (with monotonic backoff and preserved checkpoint). Non-idempotent workflows (fn-calls with side effects) will surface a retry error and require explicit user-provided dedup key. 5) Backpressure: expose a throttled sink API for batchers; complex pressure control is delegated to advanced adapters to keep SDK surface small.

Non-goals: rearchitecting runtime batching, changing server API. This ticket focuses on SDK ergonomics only.
acceptance_criteria: New StreamingSession API exported in python package under redwood.sdk.streaming.Session
Async iterator yields typed Event objects with fields (type, text, tokens, seq, meta)
Checkpoint/restore helper with example notebook demonstrating resume after simulated network drop
Automated tests covering retry paths, checkpoint creation/validation, and fn-calling semantics with idempotency key
Docs + two example notebooks added to docs repo and linked in PR
